questions.question: Which instruction category does the CALL instruction belong to in the 8085 instruction set?
questions.explanation:
The context groups CALL with “Call and return instruction” as one of the three branching groups【Page 21】.  

---

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of branching instructions in the 8085 microprocessor?

options.A: To perform arithmetic operations on registers
options.B: To change the sequence of program execution
options.C: To transfer data between memory and registers

questions.explanation:
Branching instructions “allow the microprocessor to change the sequence of a program, either unconditionally or under certain test conditions”【Page 21】.  

---

questions.question: In the sample program shown, which instruction causes the Program Counter (PC) to become 3000H?
questions.explanation:
The CALL instruction “CALL 3000H” transfers control to address 3000H, as indicated in the example program【Page 24】.  

---

questions.question: How many bytes does a typical 8085 jump instruction that specifies a 16‑bit address occupy?
questions.explanation:
Jump instructions “are 3 byte instructions, one byte for the opcode followed by a 16‑bit (2‑byte) memory address”【Page 21】.  

---

questions.question: How many distinct restart (RST) instructions are defined in the 8085 instruction set?
questions.explanation:
The text states that the 8085 includes “8 restart instructions”【Page 24】.  

---

questions.question: According to the context, which group of instructions is described as “the most powerful because they allow the microprocessor to change the sequence of a program”?
questions.explanation:
The passage explicitly calls “The branching instructions … the most powerful instructions because they allow the microprocessor to change the sequence of a program”【Page 21】.  

---

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the effect of the CALL instruction?

options.A: It is a 1‑byte instruction that loads a constant into the accumulator.
options.B: It transfers control to a sub‑routine and pushes the return address onto the stack.
options.C: It performs an unconditional jump without affecting the stack.
options.D: It executes only when the zero flag is set.

questions.explanation:
CALL is a branching instruction that “transfers program execution to a sub‑routine and stores the return address on the stack” as implied by the example where CALL 3000H is later paired with RET【Page 24】.  

---

questions.question: Which of the following instructions is an example of a restart (RST) instruction?
questions.explanation: RST 4 belongs to the set of “restart instructions” mentioned on page 24, whereas the other options are jump, call, or machine‑control instructions.
